summary: Bundle templates/ into the daemon and serve the cloud's four template routes (GET /templates, GET /templates/:code, POST /projects/:id/template-deployments, GET /template-deployments/:id) with the cloud's exact shapes, backed by a daemon-side port of insta-platform's pure manifest module (parse, variables, generators, ${services.x.url|host} and ${{services.x.KEY}} resolution) and an executor that reuses the engine's own doors (services add, service-bound secrets, deploy) with the cloud's copy ladder (<name>-2..-9), 90 s health gate, partial/failed semantics and idempotent resume. Project create becomes EMPTY (cloud: provisionProject returns resources: []), and postgres/storage become real multi-instance project services (cap 5 per type, ids pg-<name> / st-<name>, containers io-<ref>-pg-<name>, buckets io-<ref>-<name>), registered on the project and materialized on every branch exactly as managed databases are today, with the suffixed-plus-canonical-alias env rule already used for managed databases extended to DATABASE_URL and the AWS_*/BUCKET_NAME bundle. Adds one dependency (yaml). Legacy state (pg-db/st-store singletons) migrates lazily on load so existing ids, CLI name resolution and dashboards keep working.

sharedSurface.config:
New env knobs (read in one config module shared with the mode/config WP; defaults apply in both local and server mode):
- INSTA_OSS_TEMPLATES_DIR: directory holding <code>/insta.template.yaml (default: <repo>/templates, resolved from import.meta.url the way INSTA_OSS_UI_DIST defaults, server.ts:671). The Docker image sets it to /app/templates.
- INSTA_OSS_MAX_SERVICES_PER_TYPE: per-project cap for postgres/storage/compute/redis/mysql/mongodb (default 5 = the cloud's free tier INSTA_FREE_MAX_SERVICES_PER_TYPE, insta-platform src/config.ts:469-471). oss services are project-level registrations, so the count is per project, which equals per branch.
- INSTA_OSS_TEMPLATE_VOLUME_GIB: size recorded for a manifest `volume: true` (default 10 = the cloud's free volume cap that templates.ts:846-851 uses as the birth size).
- INSTA_OSS_TEMPLATE_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS (90000) and INSTA_OSS_TEMPLATE_HEALTH_POLL_MS (3000): the health gate (templates.ts:64-65); tests inject smaller values through executor opts, not env.
- Dependency: `yaml@^2.9.0` (zero-dependency). Justification: manifests use quoted scalars, flow sequences, comments and `${...}` values; the platform's authoritative parser (templateManifest.ts:7) and the CLI's twin (insta-cli package.json:47) both use `yaml`, so the daemon normalizes byte-identically and manifestDigest values match the cloud's; templates/scripts uses js-yaml but is a separate private package (templates/package.json) not installed with the daemon, and the inline `manifest` field of POST /template-deployments accepts YAML text per the contract (openapi.yaml:6905-6907), so a parser is needed at runtime regardless of any build-time precompile.
- Deploy env reserved-name rule (engine.isReservedSecret, engine.ts:341-346) now also reserves every suffixed form the new bundles mint: DATABASE_URL_<SUFFIX>, BUCKET_NAME_<SUFFIX>, AWS_*_<SUFFIX> (the existing prefix checks already cover these).

algorithm:
## 0. Vocabulary and today
- Service ids today: pg-db / st-store singletons hardcoded in engine.serviceOf (engine.ts:397-406), services() (engine.ts:434-444), secretTree (engine.ts:491-492), runtimeHealth (engine.ts:741), dbInstance (engine.ts:1020-1021), fixedService (engine.ts:755-760); managed ids are `<prefix>-<name>` (manageddb.ts:99). The CLI treats ids as opaque and resolves by (type, name) from GET /services (insta-cli services.ts:58-63, resolveSoleService :66-76), so the new scheme `pg-<name>` / `st-<name>` is contract-compatible AND byte-identical to the legacy ids for name db/store.
- Project create today auto-provisions one postgres + one bucket (engine.ts:66-126, provisionBranch); the cloud creates the project and `main` only, resources: [] (service.ts:29-58).
- The daemon has no template code (grep template src/server.ts is empty). The CLI calls GET /templates, GET /templates/:code, POST /projects/:id/template-deployments, GET /template-deployments/:id (insta-cli template.ts:310,317,386,400,407,416) and sends `branch: p.branch` always (template.ts:397) so the fresh-branch default only matters for the dashboard/MCP.

## 1. Catalog (src/templates/catalog.ts)
load():
1. dir = INSTA_OSS_TEMPLATES_DIR ?? join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'templates').
2. For each entry of readdirSync(dir) that is a directory, not 'scripts', not 'node_modules', not dot-prefixed: file = join(dir, entry, 'insta.template.yaml'); skip if missing.
3. text = readFileSync; manifest = parseTemplateManifest(text) (lenient: rejectAuthoredSizing false, like the stored-row path templates.ts:420-425 manifestOf); on ManifestError: console.warn and skip (cloud: a row whose manifest no longer parses must not 500 the catalog, templates.ts:312).
4. If manifest.code !== entry: warn + skip (lint rule 3, AGENTS.md:46, lint.mjs:36).
5. draft = rawDoc.meta?.draft === true (parseTemplateManifest copies meta through, templateManifest.ts:414-417, so meta.draft survives).
6. readme: README.md text if present; strip the deploy-button lines (a line that is only `[![Deploy on InstaCloud](...assets/deploy-button.svg)](https://console.instacloud.com/templates/<code>)`, indented <=3 spaces, outside code fences: same matcher semantics as templates/scripts/publish-lib.mjs findDeployButtons, AGENTS.md:26-28); if byte length > 131072 -> null + warn (cloud rejects at publish, templateManifest.ts:505); all-whitespace -> null.
7. logoUrl: meta.logo === 'none' -> null; else the first existing of [meta.logo relative path, logo.svg, logo.png]; svg -> `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...`, png -> `data:image/png;base64,...`; missing -> null. (Deviation from the cloud's cdn.jsdelivr.net URL, templateManifest.ts:495; the daemon has no publishing SHA and no logo route may be added.)
8. updatedAt = statSync(file).mtime.toISOString(); license = manifest.upstream?.license ?? null; documentationUrl = manifest.meta?.links?.documentation ?? null; source = manifest.maintainer ?? 'official'.
9. Cache: entries keyed by code, revalidated when max(mtime of manifest files) changes (one readdir + stat per request; 8 files).

stats(code) from loadState().templateDeployments (definitions from openapi.yaml:1958-1996):
- rows = deployments with templateCode === code.
- deploymentCount = rows.length; totalProjects = distinct projectId in rows.
- concluded = rows with status in succeeded|failed|partial EXCLUDING rows whose error starts with 'the daemon restarted' (cloud excludes platform-restart abandonment); successRate = concluded.length ? Math.round(succeeded/concluded*100) : null.
- live(row) = row.status === 'succeeded' && some entry.serviceId still registered on the project (dbServices/computeServices carry templateDeploymentId === row.id); activeDeploymentCount = count(live); activeProjects = distinct projectId of live rows.

listTemplates({query, category}): entries where !draft; category filter case-insensitive exact on meta.category; query: lowercase substring over `${code} ${name} ${tagline} ${tags.join(' ')}` (templates.ts:338-341); map to TemplateListItem (templates.ts:314-337 field list). getTemplate(code): draft or unknown -> NotFound; TemplateDetail per templates.ts:361-391 with variables = {required: collectVariables().filter(required), optional: rest} (templates.ts:286-289).

## 2. Manifest module (src/templates/manifest.ts)
Line-for-line port of the pure functions cited in files[1]. Semantics that matter for the executor:
- Normalized service: {type web|worker|postgres, image?, build?, port?, healthcheck?, volume?: true, alwaysOn?, env:{fixed, generated, platform, required, optional}}; postgres services must be bare (templateManifest.ts:227-244).
- One env name has one source across the five groups (templateManifest.ts:313-324).
- fixed refs may only be ${services.<name>.url|host} of a declared non-postgres service; generator refs in fixed are refused (templateManifest.ts:383-410); env.generated values are `${<declared generator>}`; env.platform values are `${{services.<name>.<KEY>}}` where KEY is in CANONICAL_KEYS[targetType] (templateManifest.ts:329-343).
- resolveVariables order: provided (non-empty) -> generate -> default; required with nothing -> MissingTemplateVariablesError(missing:[{name,key:name,description}]) (templateManifest.ts:609-621).
- generateValue('secret:N') = randomBytes(N).toString('base64url').slice(0,N) (templateManifest.ts:597-602).
- manifestDigest = sha256 over key-sorted JSON of the manifest minus variableOrder (templateManifest.ts:585-594); digestEpoch 2.

## 3. Multi postgres / storage (engine)
Registration model = the managed-database model already in the engine (engine.ts:850-934): services are PROJECT-level registrations materialized on EVERY branch (documented oss deviation, engine.ts:851-854).

addDbService(projectId, name, opts):
1. project or 404; name must match /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}$/ (serviceName.ts:17) else 400 `service name must be lower-kebab (a-z, 0-9, -)` / length message.
2. dup: dbServices.some(name) -> 409 'service already exists on this branch'.
3. cap: dbServices.length >= MAX_SERVICES_PER_TYPE -> 400 `branch has reached the limit of ${cap} postgres services` (services.ts:684-686 wording minus the upgrade hint).
4. id = `pg-${name}`; for each branch (creation order): {url, container} = db.provision(ref, network, name) -> provisioned.push; on throw: destroy every provisioned container, rethrow.
5. mutate: project.dbServices.push({id, name, createdAt: now, templateDeploymentId?}); for each branch: databases[id] = {url, container}.
6. emit service.added {type:'postgres', name}; return {id, type:'postgres', name, status:'ready', pg_version: 16}.
addStorageService is identical with storage.provision(ref, network, name) -> buckets[id] = {bucket, env, public: opts.public ?? false}; when public, storage.setAccess(bucket, network, true) per branch; row {id:'st-<name>', type:'storage', name, status:'ready', public}.
removeDbService/removeStorageService: for each branch: adapter.destroy(handle) best-effort, delete branches[b].databases[id] (or buckets), delete bindings whose source === `postgres/<name>`; unregister; emit service.removed.
renameDbService: grammar + dup checks; for each branch: docker rename `io-<ref>-pg-<old>` -> `io-<ref>-pg-<new>` (adapter.rename(container, newContainer) added to DatabaseAdapter as optional), rewrite databases[newId] = {url: url with host replaced, container: new}; re-key id in dbServices, bindings (source), userSecrets (service 'postgres/<old>' -> '<new>'); deployed containers keep the old env until their next deploy (same statement as engine.ts:905-906). renameStorageService: re-key only.

Env assembly (deploySecretsFor / secrets()):
1. dbSecretsFor(project, branch): for each dbServices entry in creation order with a databases row: out[`DATABASE_URL_${envSuffix(name)}`] = url; the FIRST entry also out.DATABASE_URL = url (the oldest-per-type alias rule, engine.ts:297-314). Suffix = manageddb.envSuffix (name.replace(/-/g,'_').toUpperCase()).
2. storageSecretsFor: for each storageServices entry: for each [k,v] of buckets[id].env: out[`${k}_${SUFFIX}`] = v; the first also spreads the unsuffixed bundle.
3. managedSecretsFor unchanged; user secrets (project-wide, branch-unbound, bound to this group) as today (engine.ts:329-336).
4. bindingsFor(branch, group): for each branch.bindings with target === `compute/${group}`: bundle = credentials of `source` on this branch (postgres -> {DATABASE_URL: databases[pg-<name>].url}; storage -> buckets[st-<name>].env; managed -> MANAGED_DB[type].bundle(host, password)); out[envName] = bundle[sourceName] (skip with a warn when the source is gone).
5. Precedence (low to high): minted suffixed+canonical -> user secrets -> bindings. A binding's envName may be a reserved name (that is the point: `DATABASE_URL: ${{services.db.DATABASE_URL}}`), so bindings bypass isReservedSecret.
secrets(projectId, branch) returns 1+2+3+user secrets (bindings are per compute group and are not in the project bundle, matching the cloud where bindings are per target).
secretTree: services list = [...dbServices as {type:'postgres', name, secrets:['DATABASE_URL', ...bound]}, ...storageServices as {type:'storage', name, secrets:[...5 keys, ...bound]}, managed as today, compute groups as today]. serviceSecretNames(sid): postgres -> ['DATABASE_URL'], storage -> Object.keys(buckets[sid].env of the default branch), plus user-bound names.
credentials(projectId, sid, branchName?): the canonical bundle of that one service on that branch (postgres {DATABASE_URL}, storage 5 keys, managed bundle, compute {}), route gated secrets.read.

Per-service db routes: dbTarget(projectId, branchName?, group?): services = project.dbServices; if group -> find by name or 404 `postgres service not found: <group>`; else if services.length === 1 -> it; 0 -> 404 `no postgres service in this project (add one with \`insta services add postgres <name>\`)`; >1 -> 400 `multiple postgres services - specify one: a, b`. Every dbInstance/dbSettings/dbSetPassword/dbListDatabases/dbCreateDatabase/dbDeleteDatabase/dbExtensions/dbPatchExtensions/dbInsight/dbMetricsSnapshot/dbActivity/dbQueryStats takes group from the route's `?group=` (openapi /database/instance and /database/metrics both take branch + group). dbSetPassword rewrites databases[id].url. dbInstance returns id: sid, name, host: container. runtimeHealth emits one row per dbServices entry (serviceId pg-<name>, container from databases). observedContainers('db', group?) returns the matching containers (all postgres containers when group is omitted). detail() emits one {kind:'postgres', name, ref:{url}} per db service and one {kind:'storage', name, ref:{bucket}} per bucket (name was null before; the CLI manifest renderer tolerates a name). mergeBranch skipped list = every registered postgres/storage/managed service with reason 'exists'. destroyBranch/destroyProject iterate databases/buckets handles.

## 4. POST /projects/:id/template-deployments: accept (synchronous)
Inputs b = body. Steps, in this order (templates.ts:447-650):
A1. project or 404. If b.deploymentId is given and not a UUID -> 400 'deploymentId must be a UUID'.
A2. retrying = b.deploymentId && state.templateDeployments[b.deploymentId]?.projectId === project.id.
A3. manifest: if b.manifest !== undefined -> parseTemplateManifest(b.manifest, {rejectAuthoredSizing: !retrying}); else code = b.templateCode ?? b.code or 400 'one of manifest or templateCode is required'; catalog.getTemplate(code) or 404 `template not found: ${code}`; if b.templateVersion && !== manifest.version -> 404 `template version not found: ${code}@${v} (the registry serves ${manifest.version})`.
A4. assertExecutable: any service with build -> 400 `services.${n} uses build: - server-side template deploys support image services only (build-based templates are deployed via their published image)`; type worker -> 400 `services.${n} is a worker - server-side template deploys support web services only in v1 (a portless worker path is a follow-up)` (templates.ts:753-758).
A5. deploymentId = b.deploymentId ?? randomUUID(); digest = manifestDigest(manifest); claimToken = randomUUID().
A6. existing = state.templateDeployments[deploymentId]; if existing && existing.projectId !== project.id -> 404 'template deployment not found'. If existing && (existing.templateCode !== manifest.code || existing.templateVersion !== manifest.version || (existing.digestEpoch === 2 && existing.manifestDigest !== digest)) -> 409 `deployment ${id} was created for ${code}@${version} with a different manifest - a retry must resend the same manifest; start a NEW deployment for a changed one`. If existing.status === 'succeeded' -> 202 echo {deploymentId, deployment: view(existing)}. If existing.status === 'running' && now - updatedAt < 600000 -> 202 echo.
A7. Gate (after the echo decision, templates.ts:534-538): for action of ['service.add','secrets.write','deploy'] run server.gated(project.id, action, reply); the first refusal has already sent 403 or 202 approval_required; return. (Each gate consumes one one-shot grant, govern.ts:45-47; an operator on policy=approve approves up to three approvals, same as the cloud's per-action gateOrReply.)
A8. Branch: if existing -> branch = branches[existing.branchId] or 404 'the branch this deployment targeted no longer exists'. Else if b.branchId -> by id (project match) or 404 'branch not found'; else if b.branch -> by name or 404 `branch not found: ${b.branch}`. Else FRESH: parent = default branch; name = first free of [code, code-2 ... code-9] among the project's branch names, none -> 409 `no free branch name for template ${code} - pass branchId explicitly`; branch = await engine.createBranch(project.id, name, parent.name) (synchronous in oss; the clone of an empty or reflinked project is fast; a failure here is the route's error, nothing recorded).
A9. Variables: provided = {...b.variables}; if existing: recovered = recoverStoredVariables(manifest, existing, branch): for each manifest service with a recorded serviceId: bundle = user secrets on branch.name bound to `compute/${entry.serviceName}` (loadState().userSecrets[projectId] filter branch === branch.name && service === target); values[k] ??= bundle[k] for k in required+optional names; generators[gen] ??= bundle[envName] for each [envName, `${gen}`] in env.generated; fill provided where undefined or '' (templates.ts:558-567,805-826). values = resolveVariables(manifest, provided) -> on MissingTemplateVariablesError reply 400 {error:'missing_variables', missing}. violations = constraintViolations(manifest, values) -> 400 `template constraints not satisfied: ${violations.join('; ')}`.
A10. spec = initialSpec: for each [key, svc] of manifest.services: {serviceId: prev?.serviceId, serviceName: prev?.serviceName ?? '' (set below), type: svc.type === 'postgres' ? 'postgres' : 'web', image: svc.image, port: svc.type === 'postgres' ? undefined : svc.port ?? 8080, healthcheck: svc.healthcheck, volumeGib: prev?.volumeGib ?? (svc.volume ? TEMPLATE_VOLUME_GIB : undefined), alwaysOn: svc.alwaysOn, env: prev?.env ?? {}, state:'pending'} (templates.ts:832-857).
A11. mintServiceNames (templates.ts:881-917): if any entry has a serviceId -> keep recorded names, done. taken = Set of `${platformType}/${name}` over project registrations: computeGroupNames(project) as compute/<g>, dbServices as postgres/<n> (project-level, since oss services exist on every branch). For n = 1..9: suffix = n === 1 ? '' : `-${n}`; candidates = entries.map(([k, svc]) => [k, `${k}${suffix}`, svc.type === 'postgres' ? 'postgres' : 'compute']); if any candidate name fails /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,38}$/ -> 409 `service ${k} is already on branch ${branch.name} and its name is too long to copy - '${cand}' exceeds the 39-character limit. Deploy to another environment, or shorten the template's service name`; if any `${type}/${cand}` in taken -> continue; else assign entry.serviceName = cand for all, break. Exhausted -> 409 `branch ${branch.name} already has 9 copies of ${code} - delete one, or deploy to another environment`.
A12. Quota (templates.ts:691-720): additions per platform type counting entries without a still-registered serviceId; for each type: have = registrations of that type; if have + adding > cap -> 400 `this plan needs ${have+adding} ${type} services on this branch but the limit is ${cap}`.
A13. Insert record: {id: deploymentId, projectId, branchId: branch.id, templateCode, templateVersion, templateSource: manifest.maintainer ?? 'official', status:'running', step:'create_services', services: spec, manifestDigest: digest, digestEpoch: 2, claimToken, createdAt: existing?.createdAt ?? nowIso, updatedAt: nowIso, error: undefined, logsTail: undefined}; on a retry the row is REPLACED in place (claimRetry semantics: the previous status was failed/partial or lease-stale running). emit(project.id, branch.name, 'resource', 'template.deploy', {deploymentId, template:`${code}@${version}`}).
A14. Start run() in the background (not awaited); executor.inFlight.set(promise, {id, claimToken}); reply 202 {deploymentId, deployment: view(record)}.

## 5. Background run (templates.ts:942-1172 adapted)
saveSpec() = mutate(templateDeployments[id].services = spec; updatedAt = now). All steps wrapped in try; a throw lands in the catch below.
R1. step = 'create_services'. For each [key, svc] of manifest.services in manifest order: entry = spec[key]; type = svc.type === 'postgres' ? 'postgres' : 'compute'; name = entry.serviceName.
  - reuse: if entry.serviceId and the registration with that id still exists -> service = it (name = registration.name; entry.serviceName = name, covers a rename between attempts, templates.ts:963-974).
  - else lookup by (type, name) in registrations; if found: ownable only if registration.templateDeploymentId === deployment.id; otherwise finish('failed', `service ${name} on branch ${branch.name} was claimed by ${owner ? `template ${owner.code}@${owner.version}` : 'a service that is not template-managed'} while this deployment was starting - retry it`) and return (templates.ts:926-938).
  - else create: compute -> engine.addComputeService(projectId, name, entry.volumeGib, {alwaysOn: svc.alwaysOn (only when declared; undefined = daemon default), port: entry.port, templateDeploymentId: deployment.id, templateCode}); postgres -> engine.addDbService(projectId, name, {templateDeploymentId}). Both are the same doors POST /services uses (templates.ts:991-996).
  - entry.serviceId = row.id; entry.state = 'created'; saveSpec().
R2. step = 'write_variables'.
  - generators[g] = Object.hasOwn(recoveredGenerators, g) ? recovered : generateValue(spec) for each manifest.generated (templates.ts:1010-1015).
  - serviceRefs[key] = {url: engine.serviceUrl(project, branch, entry.serviceName), host: new URL(url).hostname} for every non-postgres entry (deterministic pre-deploy through the router seam; self-refs and cycles are therefore fine). If serviceUrl throws for a referenced service -> throw (finish failed).
  - writtenSecrets = [...Object.values(values), ...Object.values(generators), ...every DATABASE_URL of postgres entries] (redaction list, templates.ts:1076-1088).
  - For each non-postgres [key, svc]: env = envForService(manifest, key, {values, generators, services: serviceRefs}); platformNames = keys of svc.env.platform; stale = previous entry.env names with source !== 'platform' and not in env -> engine.unsetUserSecret(projectId, name, branch.name) restricted to service === target (add a `service` arg to unsetUserSecret); staleBindings = previous platform names not in platformNames -> engine.unsetBinding(projectId, branch.name, n, target). target = `compute/${entry.serviceName}`. For each [k, v] of env: engine.setUserSecret(projectId, k, v, branch.name, target) (reserved names throw -> run fails with the engine message; same class of failure as the cloud's secrets.set). For each [envName, ref] of svc.env.platform: {service: srcKey, key} = parsePlatformRef(ref); srcType = manifest.services[srcKey].type === 'postgres' ? 'postgres' : 'compute'; engine.setBinding(projectId, branch.name, {envName, target, source: `${srcType}/${spec[srcKey].serviceName}`, sourceName: key}). entry.env = envSpecForService(manifest, key). saveSpec() after the loop (templates.ts:1246-1285).
R3. step = 'deploy'.
  - postgres entries first: addDbService already waited for pg_isready (postgres.ts:37-43), so entry.state = 'healthy' immediately; if the container is not running (liveState via docker inspect of databases[id].container !== 'running') poll every POLL up to TIMEOUT, then finish('failed', `${key}: the database was not connectable within 90s (last state: ${last})`) (templates.ts:1101-1113).
  - compute entries in manifest order: try { out = await engine.deploy(projectId, branch.name, {image: entry.image, port: entry.port, group: entry.serviceName}); entry.url = out.url; entry.state = 'deployed' } catch (e) { entry.state = 'failed'; tail = captureLogTail(entry) ; saveSpec(); live = count(deployed|healthy); finish(live > 0 ? 'partial' : 'failed', `${key}: ${message}`, tail); return }. saveSpec() per service (templates.ts:1119-1141).
R4. step = 'health_check'. For each compute entry: verdict = awaitHealthy(entry): deadline = now + TIMEOUT; loop: if !machineUp: h = liveState(ref, group): 'running' -> machineUp; a container in state 'exited' against desired running (runtimeHealth 'crashed', engine.ts:733-737) -> return {healthy:false, reason:'the service crashed (machine failed or its port check is critical)'}; if machineUp: if !entry.healthcheck || !entry.url -> healthy; target = new URL(entry.healthcheck, entry.url); if target.origin !== new URL(entry.url).origin -> unhealthy `the declared healthcheck path resolves off the service origin (${origin}) - refusing to probe it`; status = await httpProbe(target.toString()) (default: fetch with redirect:'manual', AbortSignal.timeout(5000); any throw = keep polling); healthy when 2xx or 401 or 403 (templates.ts:1341-1357); else if now >= deadline -> {healthy:false, reason:`not healthy within ${TIMEOUT/1000}s (last status: ${last})`}; sleep POLL. Healthy -> entry.state = 'healthy'; else entry.state = 'failed', failures.push(`${key}: ${reason}`), logTail ??= captureLogTail(entry). saveSpec(). If failures: finish(healthyCount > 0 ? 'partial' : 'failed', failures.join('; '), logTail) else finish('succeeded').
R5. catch (e): reason = e.message; deployed = count(deployed|healthy); saveSpec best-effort; finish(deployed > 0 ? 'partial' : 'failed', reason); swallow.
captureLogTail(entry): lines = engine.runtimeLogs(projectId, {component:'compute', branchName: branch.name, group: entry.serviceName, limit: 40}).lines.map(l => `${l.ts} ${l.message}`).join('\n'); redactLogTail(text, [...writtenSecrets, ...Object.values(engine.secrets(projectId, branch.name))]); cap to 4096 bytes from the head with the '… (truncated)\n' marker on a UTF-8 boundary (templates.ts:1424-1444). Returns null on any failure.
finish(status, error, logTail): mutate row {status, error, logsTail: logTail ?? existing, updatedAt}; emit(projectId, branch.name, 'resource', status === 'succeeded' ? 'template.deploy.succeeded' : 'template.deploy.failed', {deploymentId, template, status, reason?}).
view(row): {id, status, step, templateCode, templateVersion, projectId, branchId, services: Object.entries(row.services).map(([k, s]) => ({name: s.serviceName || k, serviceId: s.serviceId, url: s.url, state: s.state})), ...(error ? {error} : {}), ...(logsTail ? {logsTail} : {}), createdAt} (templates.ts:1455-1477). GET /template-deployments/:id looks the id up globally across projects (single tenant), 404 when absent.
Startup: abandonStale(): every record with status 'running' -> status 'failed', error 'the daemon restarted while the template deployment was running - retry with the same deploymentId to resume' (templates.ts:263).
Interaction with the scheduler: the health probe goes through the router HTTP lane and stamps activity; a non-alwaysOn template service may sleep after the run finishes, which is correct (n8n/hermes/openclaw declare alwaysOn: true and the engine records it at create).

## 6. Route wiring (server.ts)
- GET /templates, GET /templates/:code: no gate, no auth (public in the cloud); set cache-control after a successful read; 404 {error} for getTemplate NotFound.
- POST /projects/:id/template-deployments: the accept algorithm; map ManifestError -> 400 {error}, MissingTemplateVariablesError -> 400 {error:'missing_variables', missing}, NotFound -> 404, Conflict -> 409; the gate uses the existing `gated` helper.
- GET /template-deployments/:id -> executor.get(id) view or 404.
- POST /orgs/:id/projects -> {project, defaultBranch, resources: []}.
- POST /projects/:id/services: postgres -> engine.addDbService(id, name); storage -> engine.addStorageService(id, name, {public}); error mapping: 'already exists' -> 409, 'limit' -> 400, 'not found' -> 404, else 400. compute gains alwaysOn/port passthrough.
- DELETE /projects/:id/services/:sid and POST .../rename: dispatch on parseServiceId type; gates unchanged (service.remove / service.rename).
- GET /projects/:id/services/:sid/credentials: gated secrets.read; emit 'secrets.read' like /secrets does (server.ts:219).
- isApiPath gains '/templates' and '/template-deployments' so the SPA fallback never swallows them.

risks: Adapter signature churn (DatabaseAdapter/StorageAdapter take a service name and return handles) crosses WP3 (reflink fork, bind mounts under <data>/pg/<ref>) and the router WP (garage domains); the reconciler must land one signature. Proposed: WP5 owns the signature, WP3 owns the body.

The pre-deploy URL seam (engine.serviceUrl) is owned by the router/config WP; without it ${services.x.url} cannot resolve before deploy (today URLs exist only after docker create, compute.ts:32). n8n and openclaw depend on it. Until it lands the executor must throw a clear 'cannot expose a URL before deploy' for manifests that reference service URLs, and the FAKE tests stub serviceUrl.

Fresh-branch default runs engine.createBranch synchronously inside the POST; a large pg_dump clone (today's postgres.ts:28-31) would hold the request for the clone's duration. Acceptable once WP3's reflink fork lands; the CLI always names a branch anyway (template.ts:397).

Three sequential one-shot gates (service.add, secrets.write, deploy) each consume a grant (govern.ts:45-47); an operator on policy=approve sees up to three approvals for one template deploy, exactly like the cloud, but the dashboard must loop the approval modal rather than assume one.

Reserved-name rule: a template whose env.fixed/required uses DATABASE_URL, BUCKET_NAME or AWS_* (engine.isReservedSecret) fails at write_variables with the engine's message; the cloud's user-secret setter has its own reserved policy, so parity is close but not proven. No bundled template does this; bindings (env.platform) bypass the rule by design.

logoUrl as a data: URI deviates from the cloud's absolute CDN URL (openapi.yaml:1985-1990 says absolute https). The CLI never reads it; the dashboard and any MCP consumer that expects https must tolerate data:. Alternative (cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/InsForge/insta-oss@<ref>/templates/<code>/logo.svg) needs a pinned ref and internet from the browser.
Stats fields are per daemon (local deployments only), never the hosted gallery's numbers; documented in COMPATIBILITY.md.

Legacy container rename at startup (io-<ref>-pg -> io-<ref>-pg-db) changes the DSN host that running apps hold in env until their next deploy; combined with the router WP's hostname change this is a one-time credential churn for existing installs and must be called out in the upgrade notes.
State write contention: the background run mutates state.json repeatedly while the router stamps activity; depends on the state write lock the spec assigns to src/state.ts (spec line 251).
Removing a postgres/storage service destroys data on every branch (cloud parity) behind the service.remove gate that defaults to allow; the dashboard Remove action needs a confirm step.

Hostname collision across types: `<service>-<ref>` for a compute group named db and a postgres named db yields the same hostname on different lanes; the cloud keeps names unique per type only. Flagged as an open question for the router WP; WP5 does not enforce cross-type uniqueness.
openQuestions: Router WP: should services add refuse a name already used by another type in the same project so `<service>-<ref>.<domain>` stays unique across HTTP and TCP lanes, or does the router disambiguate by lane/port?

Should the secret-bindings routes (GET/PUT/DELETE /projects/:id/secret-bindings[/:name], openapi.yaml:6425-6607, plus /secret-sources) be implemented in this package now that Branch.bindings exists, or left for the migrate WP which reads them? WP5 ships the state model and internal engine methods only.

logoUrl: data: URI (offline, self-contained) versus a cdn.jsdelivr.net URL pinned to the daemon's package version tag (matches the cloud host, needs the tag to exist and the browser to reach the CDN). Default proposed: data: URI.
Volume size for `volume: true`: 10 Gi (cloud free cap) is advisory on docker named volumes today; with WP3 bind mounts the number may become a quota. Confirm the default with the WP3 owner.

Fresh-branch default: keep the synchronous clone in the POST (simple, matches oss's synchronous createBranch) or mint the Branch record first and clone in the background run like the cloud (needs a two-phase provisionBranch)?
Per-type cap default 5 (cloud free tier) versus a larger self-host default such as 25 (cloud pro): the operator owns the box; proposal is 5 to keep scripts behaving identically, env-overridable.
Should `insta services rename` for storage keep the bucket handle (proposed) or copy the bucket to a new name (O(objects))? Cloud renames rows only.
dependsOn: Router/config WP: engine.serviceUrl/serviceHost deterministic pre-deploy hostnames (${services.x.url}), the auth allowlist for the two public /templates GETs, and a single config module for INSTA_OSS_* knobs
WP3 reflink fork: implements the per-service DatabaseAdapter/StorageAdapter handles (io-<ref>-pg-<name>, <data>/pg/<ref>/<name>, io-<ref>-<name>) that WP5 defines and calls
Scheduler WP: reads Project.computeServices[group].alwaysOn written by template deploy and services add; PUT .../always-on writes the same field
src/state.ts write lock (spec line 251) so the background run's saveSpec() and the router's activity stamps do not clobber each other
Integrator: runs the two Docker suites (template-deploy.int.test.ts, migration) serially after merge; parallel implementers only run the fake-adapter suites
